rationale:
Evidence from iteration 1 (the best so far, score 170.1): kp 3.5 with kd 0.4 and base_speed 1.4 still ended almost every run off_track (58 of 60 trials, 2 finishes, both on the oval). max_error stayed at or just above the 0.06 m limit on all three tracks (oval 0.063, s-bend 0.0672, slalom 0.0614). rms_error remained low (0.017 to 0.025), so average tracking is fine and the failure is excursions at bends. Line-loss events fell only modestly (oval 1.55, s-bend 1.65, slalom 1.0). steering_oscillation rose sharply from 0.10 to 0.15 at iteration 0 to 0.28 to 0.31 on the oval and s-bend, which fits the Evaluator's warning that kd 0.4 is too low for kp 3.5.

Changes, one of the two being the Evaluator's conditional rule: (1) kd 0.4 to 0.6, to damp the higher kp gain and reduce the oscillation build-up that is pushing the robot past the edge on bends. (2) base_speed 1.4 to 1.2. max_error is still at or above 0.06 with off_track endings, so the Evaluator's rule says speed or recovery is the limit; less momentum into bends should let the 3.5 kp recovery act before the sensor array loses the tape. kp stays 3.5, geometry is unchanged, and line_loss stays last_direction, which isolates the controller effect.

Risk: at 1.2 m/s-equivalent command the oval mean finish time would be about 2.2 s if it completes, still inside 3 s, but the contract's roughly 1.5 m/s average may make completion marginal. If this race shows max_error below 0.06 with line_loss near 0 but completion_time over 3 s, the next step is base_speed up in steps of 0.1. If max_error is still at or above 0.06 with kd 0.6, the next step is to test a lower kp (around 3.0) or to add a little ki-free damping rather than more speed reduction.

Expected result: max_error below 0.06 on the oval and s-bend, steering_oscillation down from about 0.3 toward 0.15 to 0.2, fewer off_track endings, and more finishes than iteration 1 (which had 2 of 60).

Hypotheses to check next: (a) kd 0.6 cuts steering_oscillation without slowing the response; (b) lower speed is the main lever for max_error on s-bend; (c) with the robot on the line, completion_time will show whether the speed reduction costs more than the robustness gain.
